name: Kaiserbach Klamm
kurzbeschreibung: The Kaiserbach-Klamm Gorge in the Kaiserbachtal near Kössen and Kirchdorf charms visitors with its cascading mountain brook and dramatic vistas of the Wilder Kaiser crags.
preis: Gorge paths freely accessible; scenic toll road into Kaiserbachtal charges vehicular toll
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; gorge walkway recommended May through October in dry conditions
beschreibung:
Überblick

The wildly romantic Kaiserbach-Klamm Gorge reposes in the pristine Kaiserbachtal Valley between Kössen and Kirchdorf, nestled directly against the sheer northern cliffs of the Kaisergebirge nature reserve. Over several kilometres, the crystalline Kaiserbach brook carves a dramatic passage through a lush elevated basin guarded by the imposing limestone towers of Mount Feldberg and Stripsenkopf. In constricted defiles, the stream surges over mossy dolomite boulders, churning emerald pools and frothing cataracts. Entirely protected within the Kaisergebirge Nature Reserve, this alpine river corridor preserves pristine habitats for rare alpine wildflowers and mountain wildlife. Shaded riparian woods, level waterside walkways, and spectacular panoramas showcasing the world-famous climbing faces of the Wilder Kaiser make the gorge a prime destination for families and alpine enthusiasts.

Route & Anforderungen

The standard walk commences at the valley toll station in Griesenau (750 m) and traces the brook upstream via the historic Fischbachalm pasture (856 m) to the scenic Griesner Alm inn at 1,024 metres (approx. 1.5 to 2 hours walking time, 270 metres elevation gain). The path alternates between cantilevered timber footbridges, pine-scented tracks, and wide gravel roads. Gravel beaches offer inviting natural resting spots to cool tired feet in summer. Standard sneakers or light trail runners suffice for the riverside path; however, continuing past Griesner Alm toward the high Stripsenjoch pass strictly demands lugged alpine boots. The parallel service road is navigable with all-terrain strollers.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists arrive via federal road B176 from St. Johann in Tirol or Kössen to Griesenau, where the valley entrance begins. Ample parking is provided at Griesenau and at the upper Griesner Alm (road toll applies). Regional postbuses connect St. Johann and Kössen with Griesenau regularly.

Tipps

Enjoy lunch on the sun deck of Griesner Alm, renowned for Tyrolean cheese dumplings (Kaspressknödel). Gazing straight up into the sheer climbing buttresses of the Totenkirchl and Fleischbank peaks is an unforgettable spectacle.
